item.title: The 2026 Nobel Prizes are in the books
item.description:
The 2026 Nobel Prizes have all been announced, marking 125 years since the first prizes were awarded. This year's laureates: in Physics, Francis Halzen, for using Antarctic ice to detect flashes of light from elusive particles; in Chemistry, Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai, whose discoveries help chemists synthesize medicines; in Medicine, Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel, who figured out how to use an algae protein and light to switch brain cells on and off.

In Literature, Canadian poet Anne Carson won for works blending poetry, essays, and ancient Greek stories. In Economics, Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford were honored for models aimed at keeping economies stable in booms and busts. The Peace Prize went to Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, the jurist, human-rights advocate, and International Court of Justice judge. Each prize carries 12 million Swedish kronor — about $1.2 million — shared among co-winners.

Sources

item.title: Explaining the midterms: how does mail-in voting work?
item.description:
The Pour Over breaks down how mail-in voting actually works ahead of the midterms — the mechanics, the timelines, and the safeguards in place.

A clear, hype-free explainer on a process that generates more heat than light. Worth sharing with anyone confused about how their ballot gets counted.
